steps.thought: I will list the available tests on the manufacturing line to understand what diagnostics are possible and select the cheapest ones.

tests.name: power_on_selftest
tests.description: Boot the unit and enumerate devices on I2C, UART and CAN.

tests.name: battery_rest_check
tests.description: Read pack and per-cell voltages at rest.

tests.name: esc_telemetry
tests.description: Read ESC telemetry: sync errors, packet loss, back-EMF detection.

tests.name: compass_static
tests.description: Compare compass heading to the fixture reference with motors off.

tests.name: harness_continuity
tests.description: Measure per-bus continuity resistance and CAN termination.

tests.name: camera_selftest
tests.description: Run camera built-in self test and measure frame rate and CSI errors.

tests.name: imu_static
tests.description: Log 1000 IMU samples on the static fixture: gyro bias, accel noise, dropouts.

tests.name: motor_spin_test
tests.description: Spin all motors at 50 percent throttle: current, RPM, RPM jitter, temp.

tests.name: compass_motor_interference
tests.description: Sweep throttle 0-75 percent and log compass heading deviation.

tests.name: battery_load_test
tests.description: Apply a 20 A load and measure sag, cell imbalance, internal resistance.

steps.thought: I will run power_on_selftest as the cheapest initial step to check the basic health and enumeration of all subsystems.
steps.observation: Power-on selftest passed successfully, enumerating all I2C, UART, and CAN devices properly with no boot failures.

hypotheses.rationale: Selftest only covers basic enumeration; functional subsystem tests are still required to rule out latent faults.
Initial power-on selftest passed without issues, though full subsystem tests remain to be run.

steps.thought: I will run the battery_rest_check to verify battery cell health and resting voltage before proceeding with more expensive tests.
steps.observation: Battery rest check passed with nominal pack voltage of 16.61V, well-balanced cells, and very low cell imbalance of 18mV, ruling out resting battery faults.

hypotheses.rationale: Initial basic checks passed, but active subsystem tests (ESC, IMU, motors, compass, camera, battery load) are still required.
Power-on selftest and battery rest check both passed successfully with no abnormal readings.

steps.thought: I will run the esc_telemetry test to check for any ESC communication or synchronization errors across all motor channels.
steps.observation: ESC telemetry test passed successfully for all four ESCs with zero sync errors, correct back-EMF detection, low packet loss, and normal temperatures, ruling out ESC commutation or thermal issues.

hypotheses.rationale: Basic power-on, battery rest, and ESC telemetry checks have passed. Active motor spin, IMU, compass, camera, and battery load tests are still needed to complete the diagnostic coverage.
Initial subsystems checked so far (system boot, battery rest, ESCs) show entirely nominal readings with no failures.

steps.thought: Run the camera_selftest to check CSI framing, status, and self-test pass/fail status as part of covering all subsystems.
steps.observation: The camera selftest passed successfully with a stable 30 fps frame rate, valid sensor ID, and zero CSI CRC errors, ruling out camera ribbon and sensor faults.

hypotheses.rationale: System boot, battery rest, ESC telemetry, and camera selftest have all passed. Remaining subsystems to test include motors, IMU, compass, and battery load.
All subsystems tested so far are entirely healthy and nominal. Further tests are needed to cover the remaining subsystems.

steps.thought: I will run the imu_static test to check IMU performance, gyro bias, and dropouts, covering the IMU subsystem as required.
steps.observation: The imu_static test failed due to an excessive gyro y-axis bias of 1.300 dps (exceeding the 0.3 dps limit), ruling out a healthy IMU and pointing toward sensor miscalibration or mounting/hardware issues.

hypotheses.rationale: Gyro y bias is elevated at 1.3 dps while other IMU metrics are nominal, strongly suggesting a miscalibration.
Mechanical shift or loose mounting could also contribute to an out-of-spec gyro bias reading.
Internal sensor degradation cannot be completely ruled out until further analysis.

steps.thought: The imu_static test identified a high gyro y-axis bias, but we need to check if the IMU mount is mechanically loose or if it simply requires a recalibration.
steps.observation: The harness continuity test passed with correct CAN termination (60 ohm) and nominal resistance across all buses, confirming that interconnects and wiring are healthy.

hypotheses.rationale: Gyro y-axis bias is significantly elevated (1.3 dps vs 0.3 limit) while accelerometer noise and dropouts are completely normal, pointing directly to calibration drift.
A slightly loose IMU daughterboard mounting could cause mechanical bias shift during static testing, though miscalibration is more likely.

steps.thought: The elevated gyro y bias indicates an IMU issue. Since imu_static showed a high bias while other subsystems are healthy, we can directly diagnose IMU_GYRO_MISCAL.
steps.observation: Rework applied; full suite passed: True.
